lines.text: The door starts locked, with no wrong tries counted, and not locked out.
The door code is 4721. The manager's code is 9000.
Trying a code while the door is locked out is refused, and nothing changes.
Trying a code while the door is already open is refused, and nothing changes.
The right code opens the door and wipes the count of wrong tries. The announcement that it opened says how many wrong tries there had been before.
A wrong code adds one to the count of wrong tries and announces the new count.
On the third wrong try, the door locks out instead: it announces the lockout with the count, and answers that the code was wrong and the door is now locked out.
Locking the door when it is already locked is refused. Otherwise the door locks, and it announces that the keypad locked it.
Clearing a lockout is refused when there is no lockout. It is also refused when the manager's code is wrong.
Otherwise the lockout ends, the count of wrong tries goes back to none, and it announces that the manager cleared it. Clearing a lockout does not open the door.

Asking for the status tells who asked, whether the door is locked, whether it is locked out, and how many more wrong tries it would take to lock it out: 3 when none have been made, none once it is locked out. Asking changes nothing.
When more than one reason to refuse applies, the first one in this list is the answer.
